correctness.rationale: The proof derives pairwise height-order antitonicity, exact F² rank reversal, the two-time potential that rules out longer periodic orbits, bounded adjacent integer gaps, uniqueness of the baseline selected by sum modulo n, and multinomial orbit counts. For n>=4 the spread bound and its equality characterization give exactly n(n-1) maximal-spread orbits at multiples of n. Standalone microscopic verification matches the separate integer-composition count for n=2,...,9 on 379706 profiles and stress-tests 324504 wider profiles. The all-size conclusions follow analytically, not by extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The closest same-rule primary sources already provide abstract order-reversal and eventual two-periodicity, and those facts are credited, not asserted as discoveries. The new specific theorem is a complete labelled temporal orbit count at every conserved integer total and clique size, the exact modular dependence of energy shells, and a sharp spread-extremizer census. The inspected relevant original sections of both sources do not give these counts. An earlier own result enumerating fixed-energy two-cycles on K_n uses conventional degree-threshold parallel chip firing rather than the all-pairs sign-comparison rule, so its counting polynomial cannot imply the claimed counts. Search negatives do not prove priority; unindexed enumerative equivalents remain a risk.
residual_risks: The general source theorem already gives abstract reversal, and the novelty is narrowly the complete exact energy-residue enumeration and spread-boundary census; these might be judged an elementary but unstated corollary.
A historical exact enumeration outside indexed or accessible sources may contain equivalent counts or a stronger parametrization.
Search results returned no strongly same-rule indexed records, which limits, rather than establishes, originality confidence.

value.rationale: The conserved sum partitions an infinite integer graph dynamical system into invariant shells; existing period theorems do not supply each shell’s orbit census. The exact all-size finite formula reveals genuine residue-dependent orbit populations (e.g. 200,185,150,150,185 primitive two-cycles across the five residue classes for n=5), while the sharp 2n-4 spread boundary is reached in exactly n(n-1) cycles only at zero energy residue. These are natural quantitative invariants of a physically motivated exchange process, not a parameter cherry-pick or a known-table recomputation.
